intent: Cluster test verifying rolling upgrades: builds/reuses the most recent released Bedrock binary, runs a mixed old/new-version 3-node cluster through leader failover in both upgrade directions, and checks replication and previously-written rows survive throughout.

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest
objects.role: the whole rolling-upgrade scenario

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest::setup
objects.role: fetches recent git tags, builds or reuses a cached build of the prior release, starts a 3-node cluster on it

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest::teardown
objects.role: deletes the cluster tester

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest::getVersions
objects.role: reads each node's Status version

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest::getCommitCount
objects.role: reads one node's Status commit count

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest::verifyReplication
objects.role: writes a row and waits for every running node to reach the resulting commit

objects.name: ClusterUpgradeTest::test
objects.role: drives the upgrade sequence across both directions, checking escalation and replication at each step

misfits.why: runs full build/release orchestration via system() (git clone, git checkout, hardcoded 'CXX=clang++-18 ... make -j8') from inside a test fixture, including a hardcoded compiler version and a bare 'brdata.txt' temp file in the working directory rather than BedrockTester::getTempFileName
misfits.suggested_home: a standalone setup/build script this test shells out to

intent: Cluster test for successive leader failures on a 5-node cluster: kills the leader twice with enough writes between failures that returning nodes must pass through SYNCHRONIZING before re-leading or following, and verifies that sequence is actually observed.

objects.name: MultipleLeaderSyncTest::test
